subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@finserv.ai>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@finserv.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Anna / Michael — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick written recap and next steps to keep momentum: 

Summary from today
- Goal: Dedicated capacity to support FinServ AI production inference for our document-summarization product. Primary SLOs you called out:
  - Latency: p95 end-to-end generation (streaming enabled) <= 300 ms for typical 80–150 token responses
  - Concurrency: sustained 200 concurrent active requests during peak windows, with occasional bursts to 400 for up to 10 minutes
  - Throughput: average steady-state ~150k tokens/min, peak ~300k tokens/min (across service)
  - Streaming requirements: clients expect chunked tokens with first-byte latency <= 120 ms and steady streaming thereafter

Questions / asks from Redwood
1) Can you share a sample traffic trace or representative request mix (percent short vs long responses)? A 10–30 minute pcap/log or summarized CSV would help us size accurately.
2) Any hard constraints around max token length or rate-limits per user/account we should account for?
3) Do you have a preferred maintenance window for a short validation run (we recommend a 4-hour slot)? We suggested Apr 19–23 as options during the call.

What we’ll run on our side
- Dedicated capacity performance validation comparing GPU families (NVIDIA A100 80GB vs H100) across quantization profiles to characterize: per-GPU reserved throughput, p95 latency under target concurrency, and streaming first-byte latency.
- Deliverables: a short validation report, CSV with observed latencies, recommended reserved throughput and suggested GPU counts for your SLOs.

Attachments: dedicated-performance-brief.pdf (brief with test plan + sample metrics we’ll capture)

Next steps
- You: share sample traffic and confirm one 4-hour window Apr 19–23 that works for you.
- Us: we’ll produce a sizing estimate and proposed validation schedule within 2 business days of sample traffic.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

- Confirmed SLO targets: p95 end-to-end (streaming on) <= 300 ms, first-byte <= 120 ms. Those are flexible +/- 20 ms but we should assume strict for sizing.
- Concurrency: 200 sustained, burst to 400 for up to 10 minutes is correct.
- Token patterns: roughly 60% short responses (<= 80 tokens), 30% medium (81–250), 10% long (>250). Peak windows are typically 10–12:00 PST and 17–18:00 PST.

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding Anna’s confirmation and sample traffic. They want Apr 20 06:00–10:00 PST for the validation run. High level asks below and a quick sizing ask so we can propose GPUs and reserved throughput: 

Requirements to hit SLOs they declared:
- p95 end-to-end <= 300ms with streaming first-byte <= 120ms
- Sustained concurrency: 200 active connections, bursts to 400
- Token mix: 60/30/10 (short/med/long) — average tokens per request ~110

Preliminary sizing questions:
1) For the above mix, what reserved throughput per GPU should we assume for A100-80GB (fp16 + 4-bit quant profiles) vs H100 (sparsity/quant)? Provide tokens/sec and recommended reserved throughput headroom.
2) Given the burst profile, recommend autoscaling/burst strategy for Dedicated: recommended reserved baseline GPUs + burst pool size (minutes to spin up).
3) Any kernel/streaming considerations (e.g., first-byte optimizations) we should enable in the runtime for the validation run?

Attaching capacity-sizing-estimate.xlsx with my rough numbers — can you validate and update? We need a short single-slide recommendation we can include in the validation kickoff to FinServ.

If we can confirm GPU counts and the Apr 20 window by Monday EOD, I’ll lock the validation slot and send the test-plan doc to FinServ.

Cheers,
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity performance validation — sizing request (FinServ AI)

Alex / Aditya — reviewed Anna’s traffic and your initial sizing spreadsheet. Notes and proposed plan: 

Sizing notes (ballpark, to be validated during run)
- A100 80GB (fp16 + 4-bit quant): ~18–22k tokens/sec reserved throughput per GPU for mixed workloads at 95% quality. Expect p95 latencies in the 200–320ms range depending on prompt length and streaming overhead.
- H100 (sparse/optimizations): ~26–32k tokens/sec reserved throughput per GPU with tighter p95 tail (180–260ms) on medium/short responses; better headroom for bursts.
- Recommendation: baseline reserved capacity = 8 H100-equivalent GPUs (covers sustained concurrency 200 + 15% headroom). Add a burst pool of 4 GPUs that can be fast-warmed (container snapshot) to handle bursts to 400 for up to 10 minutes.

Autoscaling / burst strategy
- Keep baseline reserved nodes pinned (8 GPUs). Implement a fast-warm burst pool (4 GPUs) with pre-warmed container images and KV cache priming to reduce spin-up time to ~90–120s. Use request-based scaling signal and cap concurrent scale actions to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

Streaming / runtime tweaks
- Enable first-byte fast-path (reduce tokenization overhead and prioritize head-of-stream flush) during the run. Use continuous prefix caching for repeated context to reduce repeated work.

Proposed validation plan (for Apr 20 06:00–10:00 PST)
- 06:00–06:30: baseline warm-up + cache priming (short synthetic traffic matching their 60/30/10 mix)
- 06:30–07:30: sustained run at target concurrency (200) to capture steady-state metrics
- 07:30–07:40: burst simulation up to 400 concurrent for 10 minutes
- 07:40–08:30: long-response stress test (higher token lengths)
- 08:30–10:00: fallback scenarios and repeatability checks; collect full CSVs and monitor first-byte latency

Deliverables: test-plan.md (draft) + validation report + raw CSVs. I’ll drop the test-plan doc in Drive and link it into the HubSpot deal.

I’ll update the capacity-sizing-estimate.xlsx with explicit token/sec numbers and GPU mapping and share by Monday 14:00 PST. Confirming I’ll reserve Apr 20 06:00–10:00 PST now.
